rows.what the ink shows: The cancelled domain retains the loop and diagonal leg of R, a separate star below to its right, and a distinct raised plus with its own vertical stroke and horizontal crossbar. The plus is separate from the broad blue deletion strokes; the original candidate R_* omits it.

Across the horizontal cancellation, a right-facing opening bracket, closed oval 0, low comma, pointed double-stem M and left-facing terminal bracket remain visible. The terminal bracket is distinct from the blue enclosing underline.

After the equals sign the letter has a long descending left stroke, an ascending connection across its middle, and a separate right shoulder ending to the right. That descending stem and shoulder give mu rather than the simple v-shaped nu.

The letter before est has a retraced loop at the top of a long left descender and a right shoulder with a descending terminal. It is a heavily retraced mu; the descender and two-part upper body do not support nu.
After clockwise rotation, the heading has a tall looped capital L with its attached low e, then an upright b with a low loop, followed by the rounded low connection and final n-like rise of bon.

The line beneath Le bon contains separated short hook/dash groups and a raised stroke over the final low group, compatible with an accented où. The first groups are too compressed to distinguish the supplied cas from competing word divisions; three visible groups may include an extra short word.

Inside the crossed oval the faint word has an initial rounded loop rising into an ascender and a low undulating continuation. The diagonal cancellation intersects its middle; a dot and the alleged i/m boundaries cannot be separated securely from crossing strokes.

The first faint line begins with a small rounded mark and low trailing stroke for on, then shows a separate low hooked group before the tall descending p and terminal t of peut. The next line begins with a p-like descending stem and compressed r/end/re sequence for prendre. The extra hooked group may be ne, but its internal letters remain faint.

Following prendre, a small low hooked group and a separate taller double-stem group run toward the main-text bracket. The terminal stroke merges with that dark bracket/arrow; the faint forms do not securely identify a word or symbol.

The last oblique pencil line begins with a small accented a, then a tall l and detached apostrophe. The following low connected letters include dotted short stems and the taller f stroke, with a final dotted i, supporting à l’infini.
